text: Synthetic/demo frame feeds MUST be lazy (O(1) memory). The edge 'feed --synthetic N' path originally did render_frames(N * [placement]), which materialises N full board images in a list — at N=100000 that's tens of GB and the container silently hangs/OOMs with no logs (feed only prints on completion). Fix: RepeatSource yields one shared image up to count times lazily (count<=0 / None = forever). Watch for the same trap any time a source pre-builds frames.

Supply-chain 7-day seasoning is enforced via [tool.uv] exclude-newer in the WORKSPACE-ROOT pyproject.toml (resolver setting, applies workspace-wide). Set it to today-minus-7-days; uv then resolves only releases published on/before that date (observed: fastapi 0.137->0.136, pytest 9.1->9.0, starlette 1.3->1.2 rolled back). To take newer deps, bump the date deliberately and re-run 'uv sync' + 'uv run pytest'. The Docker build uses 'uv sync --frozen' so images inherit the same seasoned lock.

The edge/inference layer-separation guard must parse imports with AST, not substring-match the source. A naive 'board_reader_edge not in text' check fails because module DOCSTRINGS legitimately mention the forbidden package ('must never import board_reader_edge'). Use ast.walk over Import/ImportFrom nodes and compare top-level package roots.

opencv-python-headless still needs libglib2.0-0 at runtime on python:3.12-slim-bookworm (otherwise import cv2 fails with libgthread/libglib errors). Install it via apt in the image. The 'headless' variant only drops the GUI/X libs, not glib. Viewer image doesn't use cv2 but installing glib there is harmless with the single parametrised Dockerfile.

Edge rectification round-trip accuracy: auto-detection (find_board_quad: Canny->dilate->largest convex quad) leaves a few-pixel corner error, so the un-warped crop correlates ~0.88 with the original (a thin black border sliver). Manual exact corners clear >0.9. Test thresholds set accordingly: auto round-trip 0.85, manual-corners 0.9. Don't tighten the auto bar without improving detection (e.g. Hough-line clustering / sub-pixel corner refinement, DESIGN A1).

The edge Rectifier suppresses output (RectifyResult.crop=None, status recalibrating/needs_setup) during a bump or when no board is locatable, and FileEdgeAdapter.frames() DROPS suppressed frames rather than forwarding them (DESIGN 4.4.1: a mis-localized crop is confidently-wrong geometry, worse for downstream than an honest gap). The L1->L2 wire Frame has NO status field yet, so edge-originated status is not visible to the inference node — it just sees fewer frames. Plumbing status onto the wire / into status events is deferred to M2/M3.

LiteEmbedder (M1 lightweight square embedder) must NOT be a plain grayscale downsample: the synthetic renderer (sim.render_board) draws white pieces as (245,245,245) on light squares (181,217,240; R=240) -> near-zero grayscale contrast -> white-pieces-on-light-squares classify as 'empty' (self-consistency on the start position drops well below 1.0, only ranks 1-2 wrong). Fix that WORKS (100% per-square through the full rectify+crop+embed+classify pipe on synthetic mid-game boards): per-square subtract the median (background) colour, keep the 3 colour channels of the signed deviation (polarity tells white ink + from black ink -), append a tanh-occupancy bias dim so empty squares stay separable under cosine, then L2-normalize. dim = side*side*3 + 1.

Recognition pipeline wiring: the inference gateway selects its Estimator in server._default_estimator() from the BR_CENTROIDS env var (path to a centroids .npz), resolved at IMPORT time so the uvicorn string-imported 'board_reader_inference.server:app' honours 'serve --centroids' without a code change (the CLI sets os.environ before uvicorn.run). Calibrating from the START position yields all 13/13 class centroids in one frame (it contains every class). The embedding backbone is behind the Embedder protocol (embed.py) per DESIGN 4.6 — LiteEmbedder is the synthetic-only stand-in; DINOv2 (onnxruntime) drops into the same seam for real photos. Calibration takes an ALREADY-RECTIFIED crop (inference must not import edge); rectify first with 'board-reader-edge rectify'.

DINOv2->ONNX export (tools/export_dinov2_onnx.py): use OFFICIAL Meta weights facebook/dinov2-small via transformers AutoModel, wrap to return .pooler_output (the 384-d pooled CLS) so the ONNX has a single 'embedding' output. Gotchas with modern torch (2.x, dynamo exporter): (1) needs 'onnxscript' installed or torch.onnx.export raises ModuleNotFoundError; (2) it prints 'Failed to convert to target version 17 ... No Adapter To Version 17 for Resize' — this is a NON-FATAL opset-downconvert warning; the model is still written at a higher opset and runs fine in onnxruntime 1.26; (3) it spills weights to a sidecar 'model.onnx.data' (model.onnx alone is ~1.5MB!) — consolidate with onnx.load then onnx.save_model(save_as_external_data=False) to get one self-contained ~90MB file. Export tooling (torch/transformers/onnx/onnxscript) lives in an ISOLATED uv project OUTSIDE the workspace (../dinov2-export, CPU torch via pytorch-cpu index) so it never bloats the lean inference runtime; runtime only needs onnxruntime. Input pixel_values[batch,3,224,224] ImageNet-normalised RGB, output embedding[batch,384], dynamic batch.

Real-footage M1 validation (yt streams, operator corner-tap): rectification works on real broadcast frames given 4 corners. Recognition (rectify->crop->embed->centroid) WITHIN-frame self-consistency is strong: video1 start 92% piece/100% occ/98% colour; video2 start 98%/100%/100%. BUT lite and dinov2 embedders TIE on self-consistency because calibrate+classify-the-same-frame is a weak test (each square's centroid includes itself) and is permutation-invariant — it does NOT discriminate backbones. To show DINOv2's value you need a SECOND labeled frame (generalization), i.e. the WP-B4 eval harness. GENERALIZATION (calibrate on start, classify a different mid-game frame) is POOR on these clips: the camera is a very low/side broadcast angle, so tall 3D pieces lean almost horizontally and smear across 1-2 neighbouring squares, breaking the per-square independence the flat-plane homography + centroid assumes. This confirms DESIGN's top risk (per-frame accuracy is the binding constraint) and points to needing a better angle, multi-frame burst voting, or piece-height-aware handling (M2+).

Rectified-crop geometry: in a warped top-down crop, pieces smear AWAY from the camera position; the base (true square) is the end of the blob NEAREST the camera side. When labeling ground truth from photos, project the 8x8 grid back onto the ORIGINAL photo (inverse homography) and read base discs there — reading the warped crop misattributes squares by ±1 rank. Also: labels drawn at a cell's crop-space top-left land at the cell's photo-space top-RIGHT when the photo's file axis is mirrored.

DINOv2 few-shot centroid recognition: single-frame calibration transfers poorly across lighting (~70-75%/64 squares across warm-lamp vs daylight photos of the same set); calibrating from frames of BOTH lightings recovers ~90-95%. Gray-world white balance does NOT help (tested). Practical app guidance: calibrate with photos in the lighting you'll use, or accumulate multi-lighting centroids. inset=0.1 beats 0.18/0.25.

models/centroids_dinov2.npz is calibrated from data/eval/img_0565+0566 (Felix's wooden set, both crops + ground-truth FENs in data/eval/ground_truth.json with the operator corner coords). Rebuild with: board-reader-inference calibrate --backbone dinov2. Estimator runs ~3.4s/frame on desktop CPU (64x224x224 DINOv2-S batch).

Few-shot piece recognition: class centroids over DINOv2 embeddings hallucinate pieces on EMPTY squares under lighting shift (LOO on 5 real photos: 28 empty->piece errors, 0 piece->empty). Fix that measured best: keep every calibration crop as a kNN exemplar (nearest-exemplar-per-class), center each board's 64 embeddings by their own mean before cosine (SimpleShot CL2N transductively), box headroom 0.15 (not 0.3), photometric-variant-augmented bank -> 294/320 LOO vs 261, empty->piece 28->6. All kNN voting rules (sum/max/k1/k3/k5) tied - use nearest-exemplar-per-class. Occupancy pre-gate (edge density vs stored empty reference, Chesscog-style) is the documented next lever if hallucinations persist.

crop_squares_photo's per-square sampling geometry (projected quad -> axis-aligned bounding box extended by headroom/side_pad) is now exposed standalone as photo_square_boxes(corners, headroom, side_pad) -> (64,4,2) float32, unclipped. crop_squares_photo itself just clips+pads+resizes those boxes. This is what /estimate?debug=1's diagnostics (draw_boxes/crop_mosaic in diagnostics.py) draw from, so the debug visualization is guaranteed to show the exact geometry recognition used, not a re-derivation.

Vendored chessground 9.2.1 (npm registry tarball, sha1-verified): ships ESM ONLY (no UMD/global build) so it must load via <script type=module> + import; the three CSS files (base/brown/cburnett) embed all piece SVGs as data URIs — no separate assets. Licensing per lila COPYING.md: chessground GPL-3.0+, cburnett pieces GPLv2+ (NOT the CC-BY-SA Wikimedia variant). Chessground needs real layout size — instantiate only after the container is visible (display:none gives a 0x0 board), then update via .set(). cv2.putText is ASCII-only: non-ASCII labels render as '??' (bit us with U+00B7 for empty squares in the debug overlay).

Cross-piece-style transfer does NOT work on frozen DINOv2 features: an exemplar bank built from ChessReD (different physical set) scores 255/320 zero-shot on our photos and a trained linear probe on the same embeddings ties it at 254/320 (vs 294 same-style calibrated) — the gap is in the features, not the classifier (probe hits 90.7% within-ChessReD). Occupancy however IS style-robust (94-96% zero-shot either way), and MIXING styles into one exemplar bank actively hurts (272 vs 291 user-only): wrong-style exemplars win per-class-max matches. Consequence: zero-setup occupancy is free; zero-setup piece-type needs multi-style training data or fine-tuning, not a better classifier on frozen features. ChessReD is CC BY-NC-SA (non-commercial), keep out of git.

Server-side relative-path persistence (models/exemplars_session.npz, BR_SAVE_UPLOADS) is a footgun in tests: any test that can trigger a save MUST monkeypatch.chdir(tmp_path), or running the suite from the repo root clobbers real user state — this actually happened (a retention test's /calibrate overwrote Felix's real session bank; only the saved upload photos made it rebuildable). Corollary for evals: before using a bank file as a reference, verify its identity (exemplars shape / backbone / box_headroom) — a clobbered 256-row lite-geometry bank silently produced a false 'recognition is broken' conclusion that cost an hour of misdiagnosis.

Dim-room photos (image mean ~37/255) break a daylight-calibrated exemplar bank (~50% start-position accuracy), but appending calibrations taken in the dim conditions fully recovers it: curated daylight bank + 5 dim-light start calibrations = 506/512 on held-out dim start shots. Global exposure normalization (per-photo gamma to mean 110, applied identically at calibration+inference) adds only +2/512 on top of good same-conditions calibration and +13/512 without it — not worth shipping while append-calibration exists. The kNN bank's photometric variants + transductive centering carry most of the lighting robustness.

Start-position auto-calibration (autocalib.py): occupancy is style-robust, and the start position's occupancy pattern (ranks 1,2,7,8 full) is detectable zero-shot (>=60/64 threshold admits 1-2 played moves). Key details: the pattern is 180-degree symmetric so brightness of the occupied bands picks White's side (white pieces brighter in essentially every set); rotation detection also self-corrects 90-degree-off corner labeling WITHOUT re-embedding (crop boxes depend only on the lattice + image-up headroom, so reindexing = rotating the grid); calibration must exclude squares whose occupancy disagrees with the pattern (calib_mask) so post-1.e4 photos or occupancy misreads never contribute mislabeled exemplars. Validated end-to-end on a real dim phone photo: 62/64 match, rotation 0.

Segmentation does NOT fix cross-style piece recognition on frozen DINOv2 features (third independent confirmation of style-entanglement, after kNN-transfer and linear-probe): SAM2-tiny point-prompt masks (visually clean, 1/5440 fallback; point at base-center nudged up 0.3 square-widths — BOX prompts grab the square surface instead of the piece) gave cross-style 255/320 object-centric vs 249 unmasked (within noise), and masking-in-place HURTS (238). Decisive: masking also degrades SAME-style calibrated matching (LOO 291 unmasked vs 280 bbox / 261 in-place), so it is net-negative for the deployed calibration path. Queens/kings still collapse cross-style regardless. Conclusion: the bottleneck is style-entangled features, not background clutter; zero-shot piece-type requires multi-style training data (train on RAW crops, skip SAM at inference).

Classical inference-time embedding alignment cannot close the chess cross-style gap (fourth independent negative on frozen DINOv2): ~50-config sweep (CORAL/whitening-recoloring, ZCA/PCA, Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage, per-domain z-scoring, top-k PC removal, metric/aggregation swaps) all land within noise of baseline 247/320 (best 252, redistribution not signal). Durable sub-findings: (1) per-class MAX cosine beats nearest-class-mean by ~40 squares — keep MAX in the deployed classifier; (2) CORAL in PCA-mode is pathological (99-158/320, basis mismatch) — if anyone tries CORAL again, ZCA only; (3) style is NOT concentrated in dominant PCs (removing k>=2 monotonically degrades). Cross-style piece-type needs supervised signal, period.

Published pretrained chess recognizers, zero-shot on our 5 real photos (320 sq, GT corners, each project's own crop geometry): LiveChess2FEN Xception 256/320 (80%) — on par with our cross-style DINOv2 kNN (249-255), strong on empty/pawns but non-pawn piece types collapse to 'pawn' (r→p, R→P top confusions); chesscog official weights 151/320 (their paper itself says 2-photo fine-tune is required for a new set). Nobody's published single-style-trained model beats our same-style calibrated 294/320. Gotcha for anyone reusing chesscog code: warp_chessboard_image() calls sort_corner_points() which SILENTLY re-derives corner order from pixel positions, discarding semantic a8/h8/h1/a1 order — bypass it or orientation flips. Net: independent confirmation that style-diverse training is the missing ingredient, not architecture.

The session-bank clobber hazard RECURRED through a new feature: the calibrated-path auto-refresh made plain /estimate calls write models/exemplars_session.npz, so a pre-existing photo-mode test (never a writer before) clobbered the real bank from a repo-root pytest run — and this time the server restarted onto the clobbered file, silently serving garbage (lite 769-dim bank under a dinov2 server; symptom: confidence ~0.27 on photos that should read 0.87+). Per-test chdir sandboxing does NOT scale as a defense: any future test can become a writer when a feature adds a persistence side effect. Structural fix shipped: ALL session persistence/restore is opt-in via BR_SESSION_BANK env (unset = in-memory only, nothing written ever), plus a guard test asserting no npz lands on disk without opt-in. Ops lesson: after any server restart, verify a KNOWN photo reads at expected confidence, not just healthz.

In the snapshot page (and any DOM UI): never use a live element.contains(ev.target) check inside a bubbled document-level click handler when an inner handler may rebuild that subtree's innerHTML — the clicked node is detached by the time the event bubbles, contains() returns false, and the handler misfires (here: the correction panel closed on every direct grid pick). Use ev.composedPath() (captured at dispatch) instead. Found by fresh-context review of a 500k-context author's code — pairing a long-context author with a fresh reviewer catches exactly this class of bug.

NEVER pause CUDA training with SIGSTOP/SIGCONT: after resume the process can become a zombie-spinner — GPU pegged at 100% util while actual throughput collapses ~30x (observed: 300 steps in 18 min pre-freeze, 140 steps in 4.9h post-resume, zero epochs completed). Liveness checks and nvidia-smi both look healthy, so ONLY a throughput monitor (steps/min from the log) catches it. Pause GPU training via checkpoint+kill+resume-from-checkpoint instead. Related: on Turing (GTX 1650) scaler-less fp16 autocast overflows to NaN (use GradScaler — that's its whole job) and bf16 is emulated (slow), so fp16+GradScaler is the fast path.

CORRECTION to the Turing AMP learning (85aab09c98c4): fp16+GradScaler is NOT the fix on the GTX 1650 — measured 0/30 finite steps (the NaN is in the FORWARD pass logits, which GradScaler cannot address; it only rescales the backward), and fp16 ran 0.78 steps/s vs fp32's 2.63 (this card hits a slow fp16 route, not tensor cores). Measured hierarchy on GTX 1650 + torch 2.12+cu130, resnet18 bs~64: fp32 2.63 steps/s > bf16 0.99 (emulated) > fp16 0.78 (and NaN). Use plain fp32 on this card. Also: a wedged CUDA zombie can survive kill -9 on the PID (futex wait) — kill the process GROUP (kill -9 -PGID).

Frozen-backbone bakeoff (fixed kNN protocol, ChessReD bank -> user photos): NO off-the-shelf encoder reaches zero-shot piece-type; best = DINOv2-S with CENTRAL-COLUMN patch-token pooling (mean of middle 8/16 token columns) at 256/320 cross-style with near-perfect occupancy (0 p->e, 2 e->p) — +9 over CLS pooling on the same backbone, the one transferable win (candidate app improvement: swap CLS->central-column pooling, requires ONNX re-export + bank rebuild). Scale does nothing (S 247 -> B 250). Shape-biased SIN-ResNet50 REFUTED instructively: best same-style of all (296/320) but WORST cross-style (219/320) — shape bias over-specializes to same-set silhouettes instead of generalizing. SigLIP2/OpenCLIP image towers mediocre both ways. Failure is entirely piece TYPE (R/N/B/Q/K recall 0.0-0.4 cross-style; empty 0.99, pawns ~0.8).

Deploying a trained crop-classifier: the winning verification chain was (1) a trainer-produced FIXTURE (4 PNG crops + expected logits through the exact training preprocessing) proving the server-side preprocess reproduces training bit-for-bit (caught nothing this time only because the contract was written down first — RGB vs BGR, outside-graph ImageNet normalization, NCHW, raw logits in CLASSES order), (2) full eval through the DEPLOYED estimator class matching the training-side eval exactly (296/320), (3) live known-photo read. TrainedEstimator seam: crop_mode='photo' on the ESTIMATOR (no classifier attr) — server's _photo_estimator checks both. Precedence BR_CENTROIDS > BR_MODEL > session-restore > stub; /calibrate still swaps a bank over the trained model (covers the dim-light regime where per-set banks still win).

Crop headroom is load-bearing for piece-type accuracy at steep camera angles: headroom=0.15 (near-base-only crops) makes tall pieces read as shorter ones (q→b, K→Q, R→P, B→P) and their cut-off heads hallucinate pawns one square up (field 2026-07-18: 57/64 with every major piece wrong on a steep dim shot). crop_squares_photo's image-space upward extension (default 1.6) exists for exactly this; the 0.15 came from the kNN era and silently became the trained pipeline's geometry. Train and serve must share crop geometry, so fixing headroom means a retrain, not a config flip.

Calibration must boost, not replace, the trained zero-shot model: the kNN exemplar bank is near-perfect under conditions it has seen (64/64 on bank-adjacent boards) but collapses outside them (46/64 on a steep+dim shot); the trained model is the reverse. A 50/50 square_dist blend (EnsembleEstimator) tracks the better member square-by-square: 439/448 vs 415 (trained) / 430 (bank) on the 7-board eval. Horizontal-flip TTA on the trained model actively hurts (415→409) — don't add it.

Never use square-color parity or printed border coordinates to resolve board orientation: players set boards up ignoring printed coords, and non-FIDE-printed boards exist (both observed in one 2026-07-18 field session — a position played 90° to the printed grid, and a shot where parity would have 'corrected' a correct orientation). Chess-content plausibility works instead: fewest pawns on ranks 1/8, tie-broken by White's piece mass nearer rank 1 (autocalib.resolve_rotation). Only auto-rotate when the operator has NOT hand-placed/relabeled corners — their labeling is authoritative.

The test suite loads the DINOv2 ONNX with the CUDA provider whenever the GPU is visible — during GPU-owned training runs this fails with BFCArena OOM (transient, looks like a code regression but isn't). When the GPU is busy, run tests as CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" uv run pytest. Extends the single-owner-GPU rule to the test suite.

Bank-corruption incident #3 (2026-07-18 16:23): /calibrate trusted the operator's corner orientation, but with auto-detected corners + server-side autorotate the user never SEES that corners are 180° off — their calibrate tap then pushes color-swapped exemplars into the persisted bank (White labeled Black), and every subsequent ensembled read shows color-flips. Fix: /calibrate probes the photo with the stateless trained member (cannot be poisoned) and rotates the claimed labels to best agreement (accept only if best beats as-given by ≥8 squares); recovery: tools/rebuild_session_bank.py rebuilds from base + all retained calibrate uploads with the same verification (it caught exactly the one poisoned calibrate, agree=[32,19,56,20]). General rule: any UI affordance that silently corrects a user-visible error (autorotate) can mask the same error from flows that still trust it (calibrate) — audit label-trusting paths when adding auto-correction.

Field incident #4 + operating envelope: at projected board aspect (corner-quad short/long side) below ~0.6 the camera is nearly level with the board, pieces occlude whole ranks, and recognition goes near-random (measured h/w 0.56: garbage; 0.73+: usable). Server warns with 'very_low_angle' below 0.62 (_quad_aspect in server.py). ALSO: users tap Calibrate on whatever is on the board (a mid-game position got calibrated as 'start', poisoning the bank a second time) — /calibrate now rejects when <60% of the CLAIMED PIECE squares agree with a stateless probe (empty squares excluded from the metric: mid-game vs start share an empty middle, inflating whole-board agreement to ~40/64 and masking the mismatch). Whole-board agreement is the wrong metric for placement verification; piece-square agreement is the right one.

The inference server SQUATS 2.1GB of GPU when serving the ensemble: the DINOv2 embedder ONNX session successfully takes CUDAExecutionProvider even though the trained-model session fails over to CPU (missing libcublasLt) — so 'the server is CPU-only' was silently false after the ensemble deploy, and it would have OOM'd the next training launch (4GB card, lc0 holds 1GB, training needs 2.9GB). During training campaigns serve with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" — CPU reads are 0.6s/board, indistinguishable for the phone flow. Check nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps after ANY server restart; the single-owner-GPU rule includes our own long-running services.

Headroom sweep verdict (2026-07-18): tall crops hr1.6/sp0.15 are the deployed geometry — same recipe/data as hr0.15 gave vlab 0.665→0.835 and user photos 415→430/448 alone; hr1.8/sp0.25 ties the holdout but LOSES on real photos (409) — more context ≠ better, 1.6 is the sweet spot. Ensemble weight should follow bank maturity: mature bank (≥1024 exemplars) earns 30/70 trained/bank (633/640) while 50/50 regressed a start photo (tall crops occasionally color-flip backlit pawns; the mature bank outvotes them). Geometry ships with the model via <model>.onnx.meta.json.
